doc.title: Slide Hampton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Maynard Ferguson and Dizzy's big band
title: Life in the Ferguson band
summary: Ferguson played halls, dances and blues, unafraid to be eclectic.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: You’re doing your tenure with the Ferguson band. What essentially were you – what was your performance life like? Where were you playing? What kinds of gigs were you doing?

Maynard was playing everywhere, because he was very popular. He was playing concert halls, theaters, dances. He loved the fact that he was playing a dance. He loved that. And he loved the fact that he had an opportunity to play the blues. He loved that. Or something from the church. Because he’s a smart enough guy to know that all of these things are a benefit to him. You have to be really smart to be able to accept the fact that there are a lot of things that you can do that are going to help you to become better. That’s what an intelligent person does.

That’s interesting, because I hear those flavors – in fact you wrote some things that have a church flavor or they have a funk flavor. But Molecules is something else altogether. That’s kind of going in a different direction. So all this is coming from Maynard, that desire to be eclectic, in a sense.
You had the opportunity to do that with him, because he wasn’t afraid to play anything.
